For a North American hotel conversion where **affiliation flexibility—rather than maximum brand prescription—is the main priority**, I would start with the following shortlist.

## Best first-call options

| Brand or collection | Best fit | Why it belongs on the flexibility shortlist |
|---|---|---|
| **Ascend Collection — Choice Hotels** | Upscale boutique, historic and resort hotels | One of the clearest flexibility propositions: Choice describes Ascend as a conversion-focused soft brand with minimal design and amenity constraints. ([choicehotelsdevelopment.com](https://www.choicehotelsdevelopment.com/sfsites/c/cms/delivery/media/MCUMJCKAM4XNGDBGYQ36NVQN55WE)) |
| **Trademark Collection — Wyndham** | Upper-midscale through upper-upscale; urban, resort and secondary markets | Lets owners retain their own vision, character, name and story while accessing Wyndham’s distribution and loyalty platform. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/brand/trademark-collection-by-wyndham/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **BW Signature Collection / BW Premier Collection** | Signature: mid-range/upscale; Premier: upscale independent | BW Premier explicitly combines independent operation with a collection affiliation. BWH’s member-owned structure can also appeal to owners wanting a voice in brand evolution. ([development.bwhhotels.com](https://development.bwhhotels.com/content/developers/en_US/portfolio.html)) |
| **Outset Collection by Hilton** | Upper-midscale/upscale independent conversions | Probably Hilton’s most flexibility-oriented collection. It permits a wider range of amenities and market-based F&B—from light café service to full-service restaurants—and is initially focused on the U.S. and Canada. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/launch-of-outset-collection-by-hilton)) |
| **Unscripted by Hyatt** | Upscale full-service or focused-service hotels | Specifically designed as a flexible collection allowing owners to maintain the hotel’s identity and design while joining Hyatt’s commercial platform. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/unscriptedbyhyatt?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MOD Collection / Classico Collection by Sonesta** | MOD: upscale contemporary; Classico: upper-upscale traditional or heritage | Owners can retain the property’s name, identity, design and established style. Sonesta may also offer attractive market availability where larger systems have territorial conflicts. ([newsroom.sonesta.com](https://newsroom.sonesta.com/franchising/sonesta-launches-classico-and-mod-hotels-sonesta-collection/)) |
| **Series by Marriott** | Midscale/upscale regional brands or multi-property portfolios | Especially relevant when an owner already has a regional brand: it allows established naming and regional identity to remain, with market-based decisions for most amenities. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/seriesbymarriott)) |
| **Preferred Hotels & Resorts** | High-end independent, luxury and resort properties | A membership-style alternative for owners wanting to preserve more independence while obtaining distribution, sales, marketing and an independent-hotel loyalty program. ([join.preferredhotels.com](https://join.preferredhotels.com/?utm_source=openai)) |

## Stronger distribution, but generally more curated

These should also be solicited, particularly if loyalty contribution and brand recognition justify accepting somewhat more brand oversight:

- **Tapestry Collection by Hilton** — upscale, locally oriented conversions.
- **Curio Collection by Hilton** — upper-upscale and luxury hotels with stronger experiential, design and F&B expectations. Hilton describes both as flexible frameworks that preserve individual character. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai))
- **Tribute Portfolio by Marriott** — upscale/upper-upscale lifestyle hotels.
- **Autograph Collection by Marriott** — upper-upscale or luxury hotels with a strong individual concept.
- **The Luxury Collection** — appropriate only for true luxury assets. Marriott positions all three as operating models for independent hotels. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai))
- **JdV by Hyatt** — neighborhood-oriented boutique hotels.
- **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** — distinctive upper-upscale and luxury assets where independence and individuality remain important. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/theunboundcollectionbyhyatt?utm_source=openai))
- **Vignette Collection by IHG** — independent luxury and lifestyle hotels; appropriate when the asset can support IHG’s luxury-level expectations. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-conversion-friendly-brands-fuel-growth-opportunities-for-owners?utm_source=openai))
- **Classico Collection by Sonesta** — another credible alternative for upper-upscale assets where owner access and deal flexibility may outweigh having the largest loyalty ecosystem. ([franchise.sonesta.com](https://franchise.sonesta.com/brands/classico/?utm_source=openai))

## Practical shortlist by property type

- **Older full-service conversion with irregular physical plant:** Ascend, Trademark, BW Premier, MOD or Outset.
- **Limited-service or lighter-amenity upscale hotel:** Outset, Unscripted, Ascend, BW Signature or Trademark.
- **Established regional portfolio:** Series by Marriott, Trademark, Ascend or BWH collections.
- **Design-forward boutique:** Tapestry, Tribute, JdV, MOD or Outset.
- **Upper-upscale/luxury independent:** Curio, Autograph, Unbound, Vignette, Classico, WorldHotels or Preferred Hotels.
- **Maximum independence:** Preferred Hotels, WorldHotels or BWH should be tested against the conventional franchise soft brands.

## Most important qualification

A “soft brand” can be flexible in **design** but inflexible in its **contract**. The owner should compare proposals on:

1. Initial PIP and post-opening PIP deadlines  
2. Mandatory versus recommended design elements  
3. Required F&B, fitness, meeting-space and staffing programs  
4. Required technology, vendors and procurement channels  
5. Franchise term and renewal rights  
6. Termination damages and performance tests  
7. Change-of-control and property-sale provisions  
8. Territorial protection and impact rights  
9. Required renovation cycles  
10. All-in fees—not merely the stated royalty  
11. Prominence of the hotel’s independent name  
12. Key money, fee relief and whether either must be repaid  

**Bottom line:** For maximum practical flexibility, I would initially RFP **Ascend, Trademark, BW Signature/Premier, Outset, Unscripted and MOD/Classico**, then add **one higher-powered, more curated collection—Tapestry/Curio, Tribute/Autograph, or JdV/Unbound—to measure the incremental distribution benefit against additional PIP and contractual obligations.**
